Path: changing a running app without code | studio-authoring.draft-publish-lifecycle | P1

## Triage: first grade — `bug` · `priority:p1` · `domain:ui` · `area:studio` · `pm:queue` (`finding` removed — graded)

Triage: lands in `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/ResourceEditPage.tsx`: the load merge (`:1053-1056`), the post-save refresh (`:1518-1521`) and the post-publish refresh (`:1696-1698`). `StudioDesignSurface.tsx`'s load merge is the second host ⇒ `domain:ui`. Rationale: a spread cannot express deletion. A key the author cleared comes back into the draft from the published layer on the refresh after a save, invisibly, and the next save or publish sends it. The `draft-publish-lifecycle` item (**P1**) asserts that 「the post-publish read serves the authored body」, but its steps author and publish through REST, never through the Studio editor's reload merge. That is state ② ⇒ it inherits **P1**, and the item owes a step (clear a key in the editor over a published version, then save, refresh and publish; the published body lacks the key). `reach:` is a named producer: the Studio metadata-admin editor, instance objectui#10746.

Triage seat (objectstack-wide, seat post objectstack-ai/objectstack#6015) · `session_01W89enF2dYV7K4N2Fbfj33f` · 2026-09-27T07:22Z. ⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch. Read: this card (no comments), objectui#10746 (in flight; PR objectui#10762 open), and the three merge sites as the card quotes them.

**Why p1 and not objectui#10746's p2.** objectui#10746 is one inspector not clearing its keys. This card is the host-level cause: even after PR objectui#10762, the refresh resurrects those six keys. For any type, a key the author deleted is silently republished. That is authored metadata the author did not write, and North Star rule 4's 「永不静默落库」. It is not folded into objectui#10746, which is in flight and has a different mechanism.

**Execution notes.**
1. **Premise first** (the card's open question): does the server's draft read (objectstack `metadata-protocol`) ever return a *partial* overlay, or always a full document? Measure it on a stock boot for at least one ADR-0047 section type and a report.
   - **Always full** ⇒ the editor takes the served draft as-is and falls back to the baseline only when there is no draft.
   - **Can be partial** ⇒ deletion needs a representation shared with the server. Stop and report here: that is a cross-repo contract card, ⛔ not a local tombstone convention.
2. Apply the same rule at all three sites and at `StudioDesignSurface.tsx`. ⛔ There is no per-type exception.
3. Pin: a report switched to `joined` over a bound published version keeps the six keys cleared across a save, the refresh after it and a publish. An untouched inherited `type` is the control.
4. Sequencing: PR objectui#10762 touches the report inspector, and this card touches the host. The dispatching seat's in-flight check decides whether they intersect.

Claim: PM loop round 6 — `domain:ui` execution seat 2

Branch: `claude/issue-10765-draft-merge-deletion`
Worktree: `objectui-issue-10765`
Domain: `domain:ui`
Seat: `domain:ui#2`
File surface: `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/ResourceEditPage.tsx` (the load merge, the post-save refresh and the post-publish refresh); `StudioDesignSurface.tsx` (its load merge); `EmbeddedItemEditor.tsx` only if it carries the same merge; tests; one changeset (`'@object-ui/app-shell': patch`). Premise first, per the triage: if the server's draft read can return a PARTIAL overlay, stop and report `needs_decision` (a cross-repo contract card, ⛔ no local tombstone convention). ⛔ No per-type exception
Container & model: `S`, `mode:subagent`, `model: fable` (the ceiling); executes triage `5853761414` (bug · p1 · `area:studio`)
Clause-②: no — the Studio editor's draft rebuild; no declared surface moves
Thread-read: 5853761414
Serial constraints cleared: open-PR file lists read 2026-09-27T10:58Z (10 open PRs): none touches `ResourceEditPage.tsx`, `StudioDesignSurface.tsx` or `EmbeddedItemEditor.tsx`. PR objectui#10762 (objectui#10746, the report inspector) is in the merge queue and touches `inspectors/ReportDefaultInspector.tsx` only; this card's pin builds on its cleared keys, so the dev fetches main after it lands.

Clause-②: no — the Studio editor's draft rebuild; no declared surface moves

## What changed

Every editor that rebuilt its draft as the served draft SPREAD over `layered.effective` now takes the served draft as-is and falls back to the baseline (`effective`, then `code`) only when no draft body was read (see H2 for what that covers). `effective` is the PUBLISHED layer and a spread cannot express deletion, so a key the author cleared in the draft came back from the published layer on the next refresh and the next save sent it again.

Nine sites in three files of `@object-ui/app-shell`, one spelling each (`served draft ?? baseline`):

- `ResourceEditPage.tsx` — the load effect (`rawInitial`), the post-save refresh in `doSave` (`rawFresh`), the post-publish refresh in `doPublish` (`rawFresh`; `config.toDraft` now runs there too, as the other two refreshes already did).
- `StudioDesignSurface.tsx` — the Interfaces pillar's app load (`appDraft`), its surface-leaf load (`setDraft`), the Data pillar's object load (`setObjDraft`), the Automations pillar's flow load (`setDraft`). The triage named the surface-leaf site; the other three are the same spread in the same file, and the triage's rule is "no per-type exception".
- `PackageOwdOverviewPanel.tsx` — the list load that derives each row's OWD values and the save that splices the edit into the object's body. Bounded in-place exemption, declared below.

Three pin files, one changeset (`'@object-ui/app-shell': patch`), and a prose amendment to the pending objectui#10746 changeset, whose reach sentence this change made false (declared in Acceptance notes). No objectstack change.

## H1 — the premise: a served draft is always a whole document

Answered from objectstack `origin/main` source (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/sys-metadata-repository.ts`, `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts`), cited by symbol. A stock boot is NOT MEASURED: `/home/user/objectstack/node_modules` is empty in this container.

- **The write stores the body raw.** `saveMetaItem` ends in `repo.put(ref, request.item, { state: mode === 'draft' ? 'draft' : 'active', … })`, and `SysMetadataRepository.put` stores `metadata: JSON.stringify(body)` with `body = spec ?? {}` — no read-modify-write against the existing row (the existing row is read only for the parent hash, the `skipped` short-circuit and, on a draft save, `package_id` inheritance). Before the put, `saveMetaItem` never merges the prior draft or the active row into the body. It subtracts only server-owned keys, in three strips: `stripReadDecorations` (the read-time decorations), `stripDerivedProvenance` (`_packageId` / `_packageVersion` / `_provenance`, which the read side recomputes) and `stripServedObjectColumns` (the system columns the server injects into a served object). None of the three reads another row. Everything else it does ADDS to the body or respells it, and the one pass that reads a stored row copies back redacted credential values only: `normalizeViewMetadata` grafts a view's missing `viewKind` / `object` / `label` from the registry baseline (`viewIdentityPatch`, "The overlay's own fields always win"); `withDeclaredPageTypeDefault` fills an absent page `type` with the schema's declared default; `carryForwardRedactedCredentials` restores a datasource's redacted credential values from the stored draft-or-active row; `graftNormalizedOperators` / `graftFoldedFormSections` rewrite spellings the schema already normalised.
- **The draft read returns that row raw.** `getMetaItem` with `state: 'draft'` reads the `state: 'draft'` row (org-scoped, then env-wide; package-scoped, then global), `convertStoredItem`s it, and returns `decorateMetadataItem(type, governServedObject(type, item))`; when the row is absent it throws `NO_DRAFT` (404) — "Draft reads stop here — they intentionally do NOT fall through to the runtime registry".
